text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated quality regression detected for /v1/generate (inference-router). Metric: 'human_eval_fail_rate' jumped from 0.6% to 7.2% in 8m. Routing policy 'cost_based' is active and recent commits to variants list detected. Pager -> @oncall-alex

oncall-alex: I'm awake, looking now. Any quick signal on what changed?

maya: Observed sudden shift in routing decisions 17:02 -> 17:10 UTC. Traffic (%) to 'gpt-qlite-2b-quant' rose from 0% -> ~65%. Latency improved but quality telemetry (qa_checks) degraded.

sasha: Correlating with a policy rollout earlier: `apply routing config cost_based v1.3.1` by automation at 16:58 UTC. Possibly deploy bot

incident-bot: Deploy bot: routing-config v1.3.1 deployed to prod at 16:58:43 by ci/cd

eng-runtime-ryan: Logs snippet from router decisions:
```
2026-03-15T16:58:44Z router.decide request_id=xyz policy=cost_based score={latency:0.2,cost:0.8} chosen_variant=gpt-qlite-2b-quant
2026-03-15T17:03:12Z router.decide request_id=abc policy=cost_based chosen_variant=gpt-qlite-2b-quant
```

sasha: QA examples incoming: several truncations/hallucinations -> notably incorrect legal text in contract generation. Customers started complaining to support 17:07-17:09 UTC.

customer-support-lina: We're seeing 12 tickets referencing bad contract text; 3 customers escalated. I've opened a 'high-priority' case list.

oncall-alex: Mitigation plan: 1) disable cost-based routing 2) pin /v1/generate to 'gpt-std-7b' 3) roll back routing-config v1.3.1 if needed. Executing now.

oncall-alex: Running: `redwoodctl policy set routing.cost_based.enabled false --env=prod` -> 200 OK

incident-bot: Policy change applied: routing.cost_based.enabled=false by oncall-alex at 17:12:05

oncall-alex: Pinning route -> `redwoodctl route update --path /v1/generate --model gpt-std-7b --env prod --force` -> accepted

eng-runtime-ryan: After pin, traffic to gpt-qlite-2b-quant dropped to 0% in ~20s. Quality signals returning toward baseline. monitoring: human_eval_fail_rate down to 1.1% at 17:15 UTC.

sasha: There's also a region fallback loop observed for EU region where primary pool was low capacity and cost-based fallback picked the cheaper variant repeatedly. Need to separate region/fallback policies.

ops-lead-jordan: Good mitigation. Next steps: lock cost-based routing from automatic rollouts until we add quality constraints. Also create a canary that evaluates human_eval and halts rollout on regression.

maya: I'll file an action item: add quality threshold to cost-based policy (min_human_eval_score >= 0.95) and require staged canary for 1% traffic.

customer-support-lina: I'll send update to affected customers: short apology + confirmation that route pinned and rollback in progress. Draft ready, will share.

oncall-alex: Handoff: I'm on call for 30 more mins to watch; handing to maya for follow-up. If anything spikes, @eng-runtime-ryan please escalate.

maya: Taking over monitoring. I'll coordinate postmortem and include telemetry: routing decisions, policy config diff, affected request ids. Assigning ticket INC-2026-384.

ops-lead-jordan: Thanks team. Logging timeline & impact: ~65% traffic misrouted over ~9 minutes, estimated 320k requests affected, ~0.8% of total customers saw degraded outputs. Tagging SRE, runtime, and product.

eng-runtime-ryan: For postmortem: refs: routing-config commit `a1b2c3` and automation job `routing-apply-prod`. Recommend adding a preflight check that compares 'expected_variant_distribution' vs 'actual' and alerts if divergence > 10%.

incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Next update in 30m for handoff notes. Incident channel thread closed for active mitigations.

customer-support-lina: I'll queue proactive outreach this hour and share template in #customer-comm

oncall-alex: Thanks all. Closing pager but staying available. :thumbsup:
